answer: The mesa protocol counts N identities retaining access or reputation. Its beacon admits another only when the vault locks N+1 coins per identity, with bonds slashed for conflicting signed votes. For a farm holding n identities, the next alias requires at least n+1 coins, and existing bond requirements rise too. Each coin backs one identity; dormant aliases remain counted, and withdrawal permanently erases reputation. Wallet splitting, key resets and parallel aging cannot evade the growing capital requirement.
